- `fh_next` is never initialized when reading from `stdin`.
- Binary EOF is `b''`, so checking only `buf == ''` causes an infinite loop.

Apply this correction inside `islurp`:

```python
        )

            if buf in ('', b''):  # text or binary EOF
```

```python
def test_islurp():
    import io
    import tempfile
    from pathlib import Path
    from unittest.mock import patch

    text = "alpha\nbeta\ngamma\n"

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
        filename = Path(tmpdir) / "sample.txt"
        filename.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")

        # Read line by line.
        assert list(islurp(str(filename))) == [
            "alpha\n",
            "beta\n",
            "gamma\n",
        ]

        # String form of the line-mode sentinel.
        assert list(islurp(str(filename), iter_by="LINEMODE")) == [
            "alpha\n",
            "beta\n",
            "gamma\n",
        ]

        # Read fixed-size text chunks.
        assert list(islurp(str(filename), iter_by=5)) == [
            "alpha",
            "\nbeta",
            "\ngamm",
            "a\n",
        ]

        # Read fixed-size binary chunks and terminate at b''.
        assert list(islurp(str(filename), mode="rb", iter_by=6)) == [
            b"alpha\n",
            b"beta\ng",
            b"amma\n",
        ]

        # Read from stdin.
        with patch.object(sys, "stdin", io.StringIO(text)):
            assert list(islurp("-")) == [
                "alpha\n",
                "beta\n",
                "gamma\n",
            ]
```

    :param bool expandvars: If Truthy, expand env vars in `filename`

```python
def test_islurp(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    import io

    path = tmp_path / "example.txt"
    path.write_text("first line\nsecond line\nlast", encoding="utf-8")

    # Default line-by-line iteration
    assert list(islurp(str(path))) == [
        "first line\n",
        "second line\n",
        "last",
    ]

    # Explicit LINEMODE compatibility
    assert list(islurp(str(path), iter_by="LINEMODE")) == [
        "first line\n",
        "second line\n",
        "last",
    ]

    # Fixed-size text chunks
    assert list(islurp(str(path), iter_by=5)) == [
        "first",
        " line",
        "\nseco",
        "nd li",
        "ne\nla",
        "st",
    ]

    # Binary mode, including correct binary EOF handling
    assert list(islurp(str(path), mode="rb", iter_by=5)) == [
        b"first",
        b" line",
        b"\nseco",
        b"nd li",

        "stdin line 2\n",
    ]

    # islurp must not close stdin
```
